*Colonial Office List*, Record of the Public Services of Officers. OCR text, unedited.

**1. 1889**

TRIMEN, HENRY, M.B. (Lond.), F.R.S., F.L.S. —Formerly lecturer on botany at St. Mary's Hospital, London, 1867 to 1875; was senior assistant to department of botany, British Museum, 1869 to 1879; director Royal Botanical Gardens, Ceylon, Feb., 1880; author of numerous works and papers on pure and applied botany.

&nbsp;

**2. 1936**

BALMER, F. E.—Dep. chief acctnt., G.P.O., E. Africa Prot., Mar., 1919; ch. acctnt., G.P.O., Kenya, Oct., 1919; ch. acctnt., Kenya-Uganda-Tanganyika post and tel. service, 1933; senr. dep. P.M.G., do., 1935.

&nbsp;

**3. 1940**

CONNOLLY, HON. SIR JAMES DANIEL, KT. BACH. (1920). —B. 1870; ed. Warwick Pub. Schl. and Catholic Schl.; M.L.C., Western Australia, 1902; col. sec. and min. of com. and lab., 1906; col. sec. and min. of pub. health, 1910; leader of leg. coun. from 1906 to 1911; M.L.A. for Perth, 1914; agt. genl. in London for Western Australia, 1917-23; agt. gen. in London for Malta, 1930.

&nbsp;

**4. 1918**

BREWSTER, HON. HARLAN C.—B. 1870; took up newspaper work in New Brunswick and Boston; removed to B. Columbia in 1897; managing dir., Clayoquot Sound Canning Co.; elec. to legis. ass. for Alberni, B. Columbia, 1907; re-elec., 1909; defeated by Sir Richard McBride, in Victoria, 1912; re-elec. at bye-elec., Mar., 1916; premier, B. Columbia, 1916.

&nbsp;

**5. 1905**

BLAKELY, DONALD QUENTIN.—Clk., atty.-gen.'s off., B. Honduras, Apl., 1898.

&nbsp;

## The target record

One object per entry: `surname`, `given_names`, `birth_year` (only if printed), `education` (the "ed." string), `honours` (each with its award year if printed in parentheses), `events`, `terminal` (retired, resigned, died: year).

One event per distinct posting: `position` as printed, `place` as printed (or inherited from the previous clause), `year_start`, `year_end`, `is_acting`, `civil` or `military`.

## Three decisions

- A clause with no place: does it inherit the previous one? ("do." in entry 2.)
- "col. sec. and min. of com. and lab., 1906": one event or two?
- "KT. BACH. (1920)": one honour with a year, two honours, or a title that is not an honour?
